chapter: On the road with the Moores
title: Chinch and Ella B. Moore's TOBA revue
summary: They tour Georgia on the TOBA circuit with the Brown Skin Buddies revue; Green recalls Ella B. Moore's singing and the show's performers.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That was it. Yes. You see --
(Laughter)
-- so we went away, you see, with Chinch and Ella B. Moore, and we traveled throughout the South. We went to quite a few towns, like Gainesville, Georgia, and different places in Georgia.
Now, explain a little bit what this was a part of, this era of entertainment. Was this TOBA?
Yes, it was.
So this was all the theaters that were booked throughout the South?
Right.
Was this a minstrel show that you were involved with?
No, no.
This was a vaudeville type show?

Yeah, it was a review, see. She used to have a review. The Brown Skin Buddies was a review, but it was like the -- Chinch and Ella B. Moore Revies -- Brown Skin Buddies, see? They were -- they were like what you call stars, you see. And she was from Texas, this lady. She was from Dallas, Texas. And she had a theater there. It was called the Beaulah Theater, and she -- she sold it to some white people, and they changed the name of it -- the theater to the Dallas Theater, you see.

And because she used to travel, you know, in the South, and she was a great singer, beautiful voice, very good singing. I think she's the only one Bessie Smith ever complained about, you see, because she sang some song -- I think it was 'Syria' or something she sang, and Bessie Smith used to sing the same song. But -- no disrespect, but I think Ella B. Moore had a prettier voice than Bessie Smith, you see.

But, see, she used to calk up. She used to blackface. She was a woman, a female blackface comedian, because that's what he was, Chinch Moore, you see. I say they were of course stars. It was their show, because they had had the Brown Skin Models, number one. Then they had Brown Skin Models number two, and then they had Brown Skin Buddies, and that was the last of the shows. Then they was going to stop doing the shows, you see.
And was this in fact their last show?
Yes. See --
You said it was a variety show, a review.
Review.
What kind of things were in the review?
Oh, everything, even butter beans and Sousa was in the show, you know.
Were there other dancers?
Yeah.
Tap dancers?
Yeah. Eddie Rector, he was in it, Brown Skin Buddies, Eddie Rector, Faustin Beatty, yeah, what you call it, the Four Gob's, you had Sonny and Full Dobbs, Suddy Austin, Eddy Vinton.
